title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): X and Y are smooth projective varieties over an algebraically closed field k. A^i_alb(X) is the group of codimension-i cycles on X modulo 'Albanese equivalence'. A_Y is the Albanese variety of Y. A^N_Y is the Albanese torsor of degree-N zero-cycles, so the Albanese map is Y -> A^1_Y and multiplication by N gives A^1_Y -> A^N_Y. S_Y is the Albanese summation map on zero-cycles.

Definition 2.5 says when a set-theoretic map phi: Y(k) -> A^i_alb(X) counts as an 'algebraic family'. Two conditions are required.
- (1) Extend phi Z-linearly to Cyc_0(Y). This extension must factor through zero-cycles modulo Albanese equivalence, A_{0,alb}(Y) ≅ A^1_Y(k) on degree-1 cycles. Equivalently, phi kills degree-0 zero-cycles M with S_Y(M) = 0.
- (2) The induced map phi: A^1_Y(k) -> A^i_alb(X) must satisfy: for some integer N > 0, the map x -> N phi(x) = phi(Nx) is induced by an algebraic cycle Z in A^i_alb(X × A_Y). In other words, phi is given by a correspondence from the Albanese 'up to a bounded denominator'.

Prop 2.6: a map induced by a correspondence Z in A^i_alb(X × Y) is algebraic. This restates Prop 2.1: such a correspondence factors through the Albanese, the result proved on the previous page via Th. 1.6 and divisibility.

Prop 2.7 (only stated):
- (0) Algebraic maps form a group, and if N phi is algebraic then so is phi.
- (i) Functoriality in Y.
- (ii) Functoriality in X. More generally, algebraic maps are stable under any homomorphism A^i_alb(X) -> A^{i'}_alb(X') given by a class of algebraic correspondences with integer coefficients.

The next page carries this further. It splits off a base point, so algebraic families correspond to A^i(X) × Hom_alg(A_Y, A^i(X)). It reinterprets A(k) ≅ P^alpha(A), where alpha = dim A. It then generalizes to 'algebraic homomorphisms' P^j(X') -> P^i(X) between groups of cycles algebraically equivalent to 0: those with N phi given by an integral correspondence. Grothendieck adds the caution that a Q-correspondence with unbounded denominators does not define such a map.

Purpose: to build a category of 'algebraic' maps between Chow-type groups modulo algebraic/Albanese equivalence, tensored with Q only in a controlled, bounded-denominator way. This is a step toward treating the P^i(X) as 'abelian-variety-like' objects, in the context of the standard conjectures.
errors: Prop 2.7(0) ('si N phi est alg., phi l'est') is false for arbitrary set maps phi: Y(k) -> A^i_alb(X). Condition 1 does not descend from N phi to phi, since phi(M) for M in the Albanese kernel is only forced to be N-torsion. Counterexample: Y = P^1, X an elliptic curve E, i = 1, and phi a non-constant map P^1(k) -> E[N]. Then N phi = 0 is algebraic, but phi violates condition 1. The statement holds once phi is restricted to group homomorphisms, or to maps already satisfying condition 1, which is the setting adopted on the next page.

Condition 2 is written loosely: phi(Nx) uses the Z-linear extension, so Nx is read as a degree-N zero-cycle or a point of A^N_Y. Also, 'induced by Z in A^i_alb(X × A_Y)' needs the identification of A^1_Y with A_Y via a base point, which is only made explicit on the next page.
Props 2.7(i),(ii) are stated without proof; routine via composition of correspondences, but unverified on the page.

ideas.what: Notion of an 'algebraic' map from points of a variety (or of an abelian variety) into cycle groups modulo an adequate-type equivalence, required to be induced by a correspondence up to multiplication by N
ideas.modern_name: algebraic families of cycles / maps parametrized by abelian varieties; dual side of Samuel's regular homomorphisms and Murre's algebraic representative
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (algebraic families), Samuel (regular homomorphisms, ~1960), Murre (algebraic representative, 1983-85)

ideas.what: Factorization of zero-cycle-indexed families through the Albanese (kill degree-0 cycles with zero Albanese sum)
ideas.modern_name: universal property of the Albanese for zero-cycles mod Albanese equivalence

ideas.what: Algebraic homomorphisms P^j(X') -> P^i(X) defined by a correspondence with rational coefficients of bounded denominator (N phi integral), with the warning that general Q-correspondences do not act on integral groups
ideas.modern_name: action of correspondences on Chow groups of algebraically trivial cycles; integral vs rational motives / isogeny category

ideas.what: Stability of algebraic maps under group operations, division by N, and functoriality in X and Y

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins a systematic theory of 'algebraic' homomorphisms between groups of cycles algebraically equivalent to zero, defined up to bounded denominators. It amounts to an isogeny-category treatment of the P^i(X) as abelian-variety-like objects mapped into by Albanese varieties. The theory is only sketched; the key propositions are stated without proof.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates the framework later formalized by Samuel/Murre (algebraic representatives) and by work on 'Chow groups parametrized by abelian varieties'. The emphasis on integral correspondences with bounded denominators, and on the dual direction (maps from abelian varieties into Chow groups), is a modest but genuine early formulation. It is historically interesting rather than new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early (c. 1965–71), careful definition of algebraic families and homomorphisms into Chow-type groups up to isogeny. It foreshadows regular homomorphisms and algebraic representatives, and includes a lucid warning about denominators. The ideas themselves are known in the literature under other names, and the page is largely definitional with one overstated proposition.
transcription_corrections: Item 1°: the target written as 'A^*_Y(k)' should be read as A^1_Y(k) (degree-1 Albanese torsor), consistent with the margin diagram Y -> A^1_Y -> A^N_Y.
Item 2°: the source of φ is A^1_Y(k); the superscript is overwritten and circled in pencil in the image.
Prop 2.6 comment: 'C'est 2.1. Va être généralisé en 2.7.(ii)' — 2.1 refers to the earlier proposition that correspondences induce maps factoring through the Albanese.
Prop 2.7(0): reads 'Forment un groupe. Si Nφ est alg., φ l'est.'
